taxonomic_note: Accepted natural hybrid. Current Kew POWO gives the hybrid formula Muhlenbergia lindheimeri × Muhlenbergia reverchonii and the native range as Central Texas.
look_here_first: CANYON MUHLY ×involuta is an accepted CENTRAL-TEXAS natural hybrid M. lindheimeri × M. reverchonii. NOW actual source-labelled live botanical photographs are LOCATED at UT Austin PlantPics (Bob Harms): habit (MUIN-a), open head with ruler (MUIN-I), and collar/ligule with ruler (MUIN-L). This eliminates the assumption that no real photograph exists, but the UT use terms and whole-site photo count still must be checked before rehosting. The canonical gallery remains a historical multi-taxon plate plus parent photos until import is legal. For reliable ID: fresh FIRM DECURRENT brown-based ligule, tightly folded blades, 3–4 mm spikelets, ~2–2.5 mm glumes and 0.5–2 mm awn. Verify specimen/hybrid origin; intermediate bunch size alone is NOT proof.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hagenbuch & Lemke specimen records document Muhlenbergia ×involuta from Bandera, Bexar, Blanco, Hays, and Travis counties. Historical taxonomic work additionally documents Central Texas localities and treats the plant as endemic to the Edwards Plateau region.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Natural hybrid is retained explicitly as a hybrid learner entry and not misrepresented as an ordinary species.

best_field_traits: lower sheaths laterally compressed and weakly keeled
ligule relatively long, firm and brownish at base
rocky prairie openings, ravines, and canyon habitat
Kew GrassBase: spikelets 3–4 mm, glumes 2–2.5(-3) mm, fertile lemma ~2–2.5 mm with short 0.5–2 mm awn; measure intact mature floret instead of relying on intermediate growth habit.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Use the combination of parent-like traits rather than one character. M. lindheimeri is typically larger and more glaucous with strongly decurrent ligules; M. reverchonii is smaller with narrow arcuate foliage. M. ×involuta occupies an intermediate morphology.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Photograph an actual field-collected, vouchered hybrid plant with scale from root base to head.
Photograph a fresh folded blade cross-section and membranous ligule with mm calibration.
Compare an intact mature hybrid spikelet, glume and awn with BOTH parents at the same scale.
Seek current species-level image rights to replace the historic multi-taxon botanical plate.
morphology_keys.crew_identification_guardrails: Natural hybrid status must be confirmed with real flowers/foliage plus evidence of parents; intermediate habit is not diagnostic and parent photos are NOT the hybrid.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Lindheimer generally makes a larger, coarser more erect bunch with comparatively contracted dense flowering branches; seep muhly makes a smaller fine tuft with an airy delicate head. This natural hybrid may be intermediate and is particularly risky to force from habit-only photos. Ornamental pink-flowered M. capillaris is not a substitute ID.

field_id_finish_pass.crew_recognition: This is a NATURAL HYBRID: M. lindheimeri × M. reverchonii. Expect an upright perennial dense tuft intermediate in overall stature and foliage between the two parents, often with firm folded blades and an open flowering panicle. A middle-sized clump alone does not diagnose this hybrid: seek true collar/ligule, leaf fold, mature spikelet comparison and well-documented parental context.
field_id_finish_pass.lookalikes: Lindheimer generally makes a larger, coarser more erect bunch with comparatively contracted dense flowering branches; seep muhly makes a smaller fine tuft with an airy delicate head. This natural hybrid may be intermediate and is particularly risky to force from habit-only photos. Ornamental pink-flowered M. capillaris is not a substitute ID.

field_checks: Inspect an intact collar: the key separates canyon muhly by a free ligule rather than one joined down the sheath margins.
Measure the membrane: 3–12 mm, pointed, firm and brownish at its base; do not measure a torn sheath as the ligule.
Check folded blades and the full tuft together. Intermediate size between the parents is only a starting clue.
